_schema.mutates: true when running the command bare (no arguments), with no further interactive confirmation, changes persistent state: the deck's zellij session, a systemd unit, the profile, or any file phosphor generates -- or otherwise leaves this machine different than before. false speaks only for that bare run (the menu and / run it on Enter): an argument, flag or interactive key that escalates past it is named in "note" -- read it before passing one unattended.
_schema.needs_deck: true when the command needs the phosphor session already running, or to be run from inside it, to do anything meaningful.
_schema.note: one line of nuance: which flag or interactive key changes the plain answer above, and how.
_schema.category: the group it's listed under, one of _categories (phosphor help, phosphor commands, the manual).
_schema.usage: how to call it, as phosphor CMD --help prints it.
_schema.summary: one line on what it does: phosphor help, the commands menu, --help.
_schema.options: the flags it reads (optional; tab completion offers them).
_schema.words: the fixed words it takes as arguments, like subcommands (optional; completion). @topics means the manual's pages.
_schema.values: the fixed values a flag takes (optional; completion).
_schema.internal: flags it also reads that only phosphor itself passes (layouts, keys, other commands): accepted, never offered (optional).
_schema.takes_value: the flags, among options and internal, whose next word is their value (optional).
_schema.free_text: true when its arguments are text (a note, a question, a path): only the flags before the text are checked (optional).
_schema.aliases: other names that run the same command (optional).
_schema.module: the lib/ module that runs it, when it isn't named like the command; null when the dispatcher runs it itself (optional).
_schema.own_help: true when the command answers --help itself, more precisely than the generic one (optional).
_schema.hidden: true for an internal command: not in phosphor help, the menu or completion (optional).
_schema.no_door: why a command with a card has no other door in the deck (a DECK key, the + menu, FLEET, a pane of a shipped shape, a key of the deck): a public command has one, or says here why not (tests/doors-check.py).
_schema.card: how it shows in the deck besides typing it, for every public command (tests/doors-check.py). kind is sensor (shows live state; a tap opens it bare), toggle (on/off with its state), button (one tap runs it), shortcut (straight into a sub-screen of a panel) or plumbing (no card: why says where its door is, or why it's terminal only). state: the field, dotted for a nested one, of the JSON that its from arguments print (default --json), for a sensor or toggle. on / off: a toggle's arguments. args: what a tap passes (default none, the bare run). ask: one label per value a tap asks for first, appended in order. confirm: true asks y/n before the tap acts (anything that publishes, restarts or reaches the fleet). tui: true when a tap opens a screen of the command's own, left with q or Esc: back on the dashboard at once (without it, a tap that ends on its own output waits for q, Esc or Enter, so it can be read). A sensor's JSON may also carry, at its top level, why (something wants a look: ! on the card) and line (its state in one line of words, under the value in a box).

doctor.summary: preflight: locales, FUSE, systemd, PATH, fleet reach
doctor.note: read-only preflight checks, including ssh probes to fleet hosts.

security.summary: how exposed the deck is: file permissions, the fleet's sshd, tunnels, web, sockets
security.note: read-only audit: file modes on the brain, each fleet host's sshd settings over ssh (sshd -T, else its config files), listening ports, tailscale funnel, socket folders; --local skips the fleet.
security.no_door: a report to read now and then; its card counts what's exposed

attach.summary: get in, from any machine (also: phosphor deck, or just `deck`)
attach.note: waits (up to ~90s) for the session to come up if it's starting, then attaches; `--screen KIND` with a [screens.KIND] block makes that kind's own session in the background the first time (only while the deck is up); a first-ever run also asks one Enter before writing a small 'welcomed' marker, skipped and unwritten without a tty.

card.why: how you get in: from inside the deck you already are

init.note: the setup wizard: every write happens after an explicit 'write the profile?' Enter, so a non-interactive run aborts at the first prompt instead of writing anything.

card.why: the first run, before there is a deck; inside one, setup does it

setup.summary: add/remove machines, color, editor and shell, phone, browser, tunnels, notebook
setup.note: same wizard pattern as init: every change needs its own Enter, aborting on EOF before anything is written.

panel.summary: the DECK tab: state, next steps, every action one key away
panel.note: the DECK tab: needs a tty, and every action needs its own keypress; the riskiest ones (restart, update, web on, f: apply a hand-edited profile) ask to confirm first; o (theme) writes the profile only on Enter in its picker. n opens push, voice and trace, whose own screens change the profile or a trace only on a keypress.

card.why: it is the DECK tab itself

commands.summary: every phosphor command, browsable by category
commands.note: a category/command picker; a read-only leaf runs on Enter (this same file decides which), and so do the ones that ask for what they need on their own screen (ask, broadcast, send, clip, receive, triage, face, push, tts, trace, read -- any change still asks there); anything else just copies its usage line -- never guesses at missing arguments.

phone.summary: put a phone or tablet one tap away from the deck
phone.note: prints instructions or a kit script for a new screen; the real changes (keys, ~/.local/bin/deck) happen on that remote device when the printed script runs there, not here.

screen.summary: the same kit as phone, for a computer without Termux
screen.note: same as phone: prints a kit script (`--as KIND` only changes what its deck command says); the real changes happen on the remote device that runs it.

gen.note: writes zellij/yazi/btop/gping/ctop config, layouts, systemd units and mounts, and restarts fleet mounts if rclone.conf changed; --dry-run writes nothing.

card.why: the DECK tab's f applies a changed profile: gen and a restart together

up.summary: start the deck (and at every boot)
up.note: enables and starts the session, timer and mount units, unconditionally.

card.why: starts the deck: from inside it, it is already up

update.summary: a newer version: pull or copy, install, restart
update.note: pulls or copies the new code, runs the installer, and by default restarts the live session (or hotswaps it) with no confirmation; --no-restart is the only opt-out.

version.summary: this version, whether there's a newer one, and what it brings
version.note: reads a small local cache; --check also does a `git fetch` (network only, no local mutation).

restart.summary: bring the session down cleanly and back up
restart.note: down then up, unconditionally, no confirmation; run from inside the live session it detaches and finishes in the background.

down.note: stops the session and its timer/service units and reaps leftover processes, unconditionally.

card.why: stops the deck you would be tapping it from

workspace.summary: a tab per idea: folder, git, its assistants
workspace.note: `list` (the default off a terminal, --json too) is read-only, and so is the bare panel on one, except its n (the same as `new`) and its x (the same as `rm`); `rm` takes the tab out of the profile, closes it and moves the folder into the trash, asking first (`--yes` without a terminal); `open` needs the deck ($ZELLIJ) to actually switch tabs, otherwise it just prints; `new` creates the folder, commits it, adds the tab to the profile and regenerates -- non-interactively it also skips the 'folder already has stuff in it' check.

ask.summary: a one-shot question to whichever assistant CLI is installed, no tab; -c adds your latest notes
ask.note: shells out to an installed assistant CLI for one answer and prints it; nothing is written locally. -c reads the notebook and sends its latest decisions and summaries along.
ask.no_door: the assistants' own tool: triage (g in DECK) asks through it; its card or a shell for the rest

mcp.summary: the deck, read-only, for an assistant that speaks MCP: glance, fleet, notes, workspaces, logs
mcp.note: an MCP server on stdin/stdout, started by an assistant and gone when it closes the pipe; listens on no port. Its tools (glance, fleet, notes, workspaces, logs) only read local files -- fleet reads fleet.json, no ssh -- and none sends, restarts or writes. On a terminal it prints its help and exits.

card.why: an assistant starts it over stdio; nobody reads it

read.summary: a web page as plain text, or a web search to pick one from; --ask hands it to an assistant
read.note: fetches a web page (or searches DuckDuckGo with the words given) and prints or pages its text; nothing is written. --ask sends the page and the question to an installed assistant CLI with no tools; the search words and the page's address leave the brain.

note.usage: phosphor note [--kind KIND] [--by NAME] [--book NAME | --file PATH] [--tab TAB] [--project NAME] [--here] TEXT | -
note.summary: add a note to the shared notebook
note.note: appends to the shared notebook on every invocation, no confirmation; with no --project, one written from a workspace's folder or tab is filed under that workspace, else under the project of the last note from that tab; with [notes] require_project = true it refuses (exit 2) a note it can't file, listing the projects in use and the workspaces.

notes.usage: phosphor notes [--book NAME | --file PATH] [--tab TAB] [--project NAME] [--archive]
notes.summary: read it (newest first); pick one to edit, archive, chat
notes.note: plain/non-interactive is read-only; the interactive viewer's write/edit/archive/done/restore/chat/workspace/move keys each mutate on one keypress, mostly with no secondary confirm ('D', delete for good, does ask first).

digest.summary: the last day (commits, fleet trouble, notes, todos) as one summary note, written by an assistant
digest.note: collects the last day's commits, FLEET history, notes and todos, sends them to an installed assistant CLI (no tools) and appends its answer to the notebook as a summary note, no confirmation; --print only prints what it collected and sends nothing; a day with nothing in it writes nothing.
digest.no_door: a summary note written on demand or by a script: no screen of its own, its card runs it

fleet.note: the SYS fleet panel: reads hosts over ssh, but its background watchdog also self-heals a dead ~/fleet mount on its own (fusermount, then a systemctl restart) and calls phosphor notify on a host's up/down flip. --json only reads fleet.json (its cache) and starts nothing. Its s/l/t keys open a tab (ssh, logs, triage) and change nothing on the host; h draws a host's last 24 hours in the same pane. The deck's own fleet also keeps that history in ~/.cache/phosphor/history.json.

glance.summary: fleet, unread mentions, open todos -- for a small screen
glance.note: a summary from local cache files (fleet, mentions, notes, workspace status); --once, --json and --serve only read. The screen that stays up writes only from an item's page, on Enter over an action other than back (the default): done archives that todo in the notebook, all read marks the mentions read. --serve listens (tailnet only, token; --lan: the LAN address instead) until Ctrl-C, answers the JSON, the SolarOS app (/solaros.py) and its /menu to that token (the app also to /p/CODE, a code phosphor solaros on prints, good once for 10 minutes), and makes its token file the first time (--new-token replaces it). Two POSTs from that app write a file each and nothing else: /pair a key waiting for phosphor solaros pair's Enter, /open which menu entry the panel's next ssh session starts on.
glance.no_door: the screen a small gadget shows (phones manual, "A glance instead of the whole deck")

solaros.usage: phosphor solaros [status [--json] | on | off | pair | forget]
solaros.summary: a SolarOS panel as a face of the deck: one switch, its lines on the clipboard, a menu over ssh
solaros.note: status (the default) only reads. on writes [glance] serve = "lan" to the profile and starts a user service (phosphor-glance.service) serving glance on the LAN behind its token, and puts the panel's two lines on the clipboard; off stops and removes it. pair opens a 10-minute window and waits: a panel's key goes into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (forced to the panel's menu whatever it asks to run, though the deck's tabs it opens take what's typed; the old file kept as .bak.solaros) only on your Enter after both screens show the same fingerprint. forget takes every paired panel's key out. session is what that key runs: the deck's tabs one at a time, phosphor's screens run there and the rest mirrored (hidden), and fleet its FLEET tab (hidden).

mirror.summary: one pane, for a screen too slow for zellij: changed lines only, no color, keys go back
mirror.note: reads one pane of the deck's session (zellij action dump-screen, no client attached) and paints only what changed, at the pace the screen's link takes; every key typed on it goes into that pane (zellij action write), unconfirmed, as if typed there: Ctrl-C included, only Ctrl-] stays with mirror (it leaves). --view sends no key (q or Ctrl-C leave too); --once prints one frame and changes nothing. With neither --tab nor --pane it lists the session's panes and exits 2.

card.why: a slow screen's ssh key runs it, on a tab or pane it names

adjutant.summary: the SYS panel that speaks up
adjutant.note: SYS display of local fleet/notes state; its zellij calls (jump to a tab, hide a toast) only fire on a keypress and are no-ops without a live session.

card.why: it is the SYS pane that speaks; notify is its card

notify.summary: send the adjutant a message (and your phone, with [push])
notify.note: writes one ephemeral events-file line; pushes or speaks only if [push]/[tts] are already on -- no session, systemd or profile change.
notify.no_door: for scripts and assistants: how they tell you something

tts.summary: speak notifications aloud with selectable voices
tts.note: speaking a message or checking status changes nothing; `install` downloads and installs a TTS engine, and `on`/`off` rewrite [tts] in the profile.

push.summary: [push] status, or --qr: a subscribe link/QR for the phone's ntfy app
push.note: status/--qr only read the profile and print/clip a URL; `on`/`off` (or o on its screen) rewrite [push] in the profile, `on` making up a topic if there's none; the actual send only happens from `phosphor notify`.

usage.summary: how much of your Claude Code / Antigravity plan is used, and when it refills
usage.note: read-only: reads the token claude/agy already keep and asks that provider for its usage; never refreshes a token.

prom.summary: Prometheus gauge dashboard (see [prometheus] in the profile)

services.summary: systemd units and their state: phosphor's own, plus any you add
services.note: --once, --json and non-tty are read-only; on a terminal the panel's r (restart) and s (start/stop) act on the picked unit after a y confirm, through sudo for a system unit.

containers.summary: a host's docker/podman containers: logs, restart, start/stop
containers.note: --once, --json and non-tty are read-only (a docker/podman ps over ssh); on a terminal the panel's r (restart) and s (start/stop) act on the picked container on that host after a y confirm.

review.summary: open merge/pull requests: CI, conflicts, diff, try the branch
review.note: listing/diffing is read-only; the interactive 't' (checkout into its own worktree) and 'x' (drop it) mutate on a keypress -- your own working copy is never touched.

screens.summary: who's attached (phone, tablet, another computer); kick one loose
screens.note: listing (--list, --json) is read-only; kicking a screen loose ('x') asks y/n first, on purpose; 'o', after its own y/n, writes or removes a [screens.KIND] block in the profile (backup first), runs phosphor gen, kicks that kind's screens and, when sharing again, closes the kind's own session.

mem.summary: how much memory each tab and pane of the deck takes, heaviest first
mem.note: read-only: reads /proc and asks zellij for its pane list; with the deck down it says so.

panels.summary: your own panels: a Python file in panels.d, on the same kit as every panel
panels.note: plain and --json only list panels.d's files (their docstrings read, never run); `phosphor panels NAME` runs that file, user code, like a cmd in apps.toml: what it can change is up to the file.
panels.no_door: your panels.d panels go where you put them (Alt-r); this only lists them

dash.summary: a dashboard of your own: the cards you pick, each with its live value; + adds one (also: phosphor cards)
dash.note: bare it only shows cards, a box each filling the pane (none: the gallery opens); a key or tap zooms the pane and runs that card as its own card says, asking first where it would publish or restart. Piped, it prints one line per card, once. In a profile tab (gen passes --tab) adding or taking away a card rewrites that tab in deck.toml (a .bak first) and runs gen; --json only reads.

card.why: it is the dashboard: cards in the + menu opens it

keys.summary: key guide, updates itself when you install a tool
keys.note: read-only key guide (its interactive 's' just launches phosphor setup).

store.summary: install TUIs from their releases, no sudo; open what you have
store.note: listing is read-only; picking an uninstalled app in the interactive picker downloads and installs it immediately, no confirm ('d', remove, does ask first).

new.summary: the + menu: a shell, a machine, an assistant, your apps, a layout
new.note: with no `--here`: lists (non-tty) or opens a picker that adds a tab on selection; `--here` (what Alt-n and the + menu actually run) refuses instead of adding a tab if nobody's attached to the session (zellij action list-clients names none).

keep.summary: write a tab you arranged by hand into your profile
keep.note: reading the tab needs the deck (zellij dump-layout); writing it into the profile needs its own explicit 'keep it?' Enter, aborting instead of writing without one.

tabs.summary: the tabs your profile brings back: forget one, reorder, reopen
tabs.note: listing is read-only; `--forget NAME` mutates unconditionally, and the interactive view's forget asks y/n first, its reorder (K/J) and reopen (o) keys mutate on one keypress.

migrate.summary: bring an older profile up to date: a diff of each change first, a backup kept
migrate.note: shows each pending profile change as a diff; writing it (and version in [deck]) needs its own explicit 'write it?' Enter, aborting instead of writing without one; --dry-run only shows. A profile written by a newer phosphor is never touched.

backup.summary: the brain's own backup: profile, tabs.d, notebook, glance token, in one file
backup.note: only writes a new archive file (0600; refuses one that's already there); reads the profile, tabs.d, notebook, glance token and faces, never ~/.ssh.

restore.summary: put a backup back: what it writes first, one y/n, a .bak of what it replaces
restore.note: shows each file the backup would write as new, replace or same; writing them (the profile through write_profile, a .bak for anything replaced) needs its own explicit 'restore it?' Enter, aborting instead of writing without one; --dry-run only shows. Ends with phosphor gen --dry-run, never a real gen.
restore.no_door: it takes a backup file and replaces what's there: typed, or from its card

recipe.summary: starter tab bundles: homelab, dev, bubble, workbench
recipe.note: with no NAME: lists what's already added (read-only, though the interactive picker adds on selection with no confirm); `phosphor recipe NAME` drops the bundle into tabs.d and regenerates unconditionally, then (on a terminal, after a y) installs the store-carried programs it runs into ~/.local/bin; `--remove NAME` deletes that file (and any stub `phosphor tabs` placed for it) and regenerates.

shortcuts.summary: the deck's keys, yours to change; updates never reset them
shortcuts.note: --kdl and non-tty are read-only; the interactive picker writes [keys] and regenerates once a new key is captured.

theme.summary: the deck's color: p31, p3, p4, ega, paper, previewed before it's saved
theme.note: --list, and the picker until Enter, are read-only; `theme NAME` writes [deck] theme (backup kept) and applies nothing; the picker's Enter saves, runs gen and asks before a restart.

edit.summary: what Alt-r runs: unlock a tab, change it, save it or put it back
edit.note: needs to run inside the deck ($ZELLIJ); the first step already unlocks and renames the tab, and every action after (save, put back, swap, split, close) mutates the tab or profile on one keypress, no further confirmation.

card.why: Alt-r runs it on the tab you are on; a card has no tab of its own

mentions.summary: read-only feed of chat notifications; --setup hooks matterhorn
mentions.note: the plain feed is read-only; `--setup` unconditionally writes a hook script and rewrites Mattermost's config.ini; the interactive viewer mutates (marks seen, runs `prepare`) on a keypress.

clip.summary: a file or a pipe onto your device's clipboard
clip.note: sends to every attached screen's OSC 52 clipboard; `--save FILE` writes that file locally instead.

card.why: takes a file or a pipe, from a shell

send.summary: one real file, as a one-time link and QR; gone once it's downloaded
send.note: opens a real (if temporary) HTTP listener serving the file until it's downloaded or the timeout passes.

receive.summary: the other way: a one-time upload link, into ~/received
receive.note: opens a one-time HTTP upload link/QR (LAN or tailnet, never the internet); the uploaded file lands in ~/received (or --dir) the moment someone sends one, and it stops the instant that happens or after --timeout.

web.usage: phosphor web on [--yes] | off | status [--json] | token
web.summary: on / off / status / token: the deck in a browser, tailnet only
web.note: status (the default) is read-only; `on` writes [deck].web, regenerates, and publishes a tailnet HTTPS endpoint, then pauses for Enter and restarts the live session -- without a tty it publishes but does NOT restart unless --yes is also given; `off`/`token` mutate unconditionally.

card.why: turns a ~/fleet path into host:path, for scripts and yazi

tail.summary: stream a fleet host's journalctl/docker/podman logs, reconnecting on its own
tail.note: just a normal ssh tab with the journalctl/docker/podman command already filled in, through `phosphor run --reconnect` -- read-only, reconnects on a dropped link the same way any ssh tab already does.

triage.summary: a diagnostic snapshot of a host, piped straight to phosphor ask
triage.note: with no HOST: lists what the fleet panel is already flagging (read-only, same data phosphor glance uses); with one, collects a snapshot over ssh and shells out to an assistant CLI the same way phosphor ask does -- nothing is written, locally or on the remote host.

upkeep.summary: upgrade or reboot a fleet machine, in the open: says what it runs and waits for you
upkeep.note: bare it only prints usage. With a HOST it prints the command, then waits: Enter runs an upgrade, the host's name typed runs a reboot; only then does it change the host (ssh -t, sudo asking in the same terminal). Without a terminal it refuses and nothing runs.

broadcast.usage: phosphor broadcast [--host NAME]... [--role ROLE] [--timeout S] [--rolling [--pause S]] [--yes] -- COMMAND
broadcast.summary: one command on every fleet host at once, output grouped by host
broadcast.note: runs an arbitrary command over ssh on every fleet host (or --host/--role): it can change anything there. Asks first on a terminal; without one it refuses unless --yes is given. --rolling goes host by host and stops at the first failure; on a terminal it asks before each next host, with --yes it goes on by itself.
broadcast.no_door: one command line on every host at once: typed on purpose, or from its card

tunnel.summary: keep your ssh config's LocalForward tunnels up
tunnel.note: listing (and --json) is read-only; `on HOST`/`off HOST` write the profile and start/stop a systemd unit that keeps `ssh -N HOST` running, unconditionally. On a terminal with no HOST, its panel does the same for the picked host on Enter, after a y/n.

face.usage: phosphor face IMAGE [--name NAME] [--w N] [--h N]
face.summary: turn an image into the adjutant's face

card.why: takes an image file and its sizes, from a shell

logs.summary: the deck's own log: crashes, hangs, exits, restarts; -f follows
logs.note: read-only tail of the deck's own log.

trace.summary: verbose logging for one tool, for about 30 minutes
trace.note: with no TOOL: lists what's tracing (read-only); `phosphor trace TOOL` writes a trace-control file that expires itself in about 30 minutes. `off TOOL` removes it sooner; on a terminal with no TOOL, its screen starts or stops one on a keypress.

stats.summary: which phosphor commands get run here, counted on this machine only
stats.note: read-only; --clear deletes the counts (~/.cache/phosphor/stats.json) and starts again from today.
stats.no_door: numbers for deciding what to remove: its card is enough

demo.summary: a throwaway session over made-up machines, for a screenshot
demo.note: starts (or, with --stop, tears down) a separate throwaway zellij session and its own cache state -- isolated from your real profile/session, but a real one while it runs; --tour adds a floating guide on each of its tabs, only ever in that session.

card.why: a throwaway session for a screenshot, from a terminal

privacy.summary: before you push a fork: finds your own data in it

card.why: a git hook and a check before you push a fork

completion.summary: tab completion for bash or zsh

card.why: its output goes into a shell's rc file

help.summary: the manual, by topic; phosphor docs rebuilds AGENTS.md
help.note: prints the command list, or one manual page in a pager; changes nothing.

run.summary: what a tab's pane runs: the program, and what happens when it ends
run.note: internal: the wrapper every layout pane starts through; run by hand it only runs COMMAND in this terminal.

mention-hook.summary: what matterhorn calls with one notification, as JSON on stdin
mention-hook.note: internal: appends the notification to the mentions feed and notifies; never prints.

docs.note: maintainers: rewrites AGENTS.md in this checkout; --check only says whether it's stale.
